A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EpiCoder work and provide readable main text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables and Appendices A–C. Content can be reliably matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original EpiCoder benchmark evaluations, repository-generation examples, and scaling, complexity and diversity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including EpiCoder benchmark scores and the analyses in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A retain the same feature extraction, evolution, reweighted sampling, code generation and test-guided refinement procedures. Algorithms 1–2 and the model choices are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training sources and task coverage are unchanged. Both evaluate HumanEval/MBPP and their Plus tests, BigCodeBench, EvoEval, the English Python subset of FullStackBench, and XFileDep, and retain the repository-generation example.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1, Figure 4 and Tables 5–8. In particular, Tables 5–6 retain Magicoder-DS, WaveCoder-Ultra-6.7B and SelfCodeAlign-CQ-7B; the complexity/diversity comparison datasets also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The synthesis sizes, model configurations, subset-training experiments and evaluation procedures are retained. XFileDep still uses 466 problems, pass@1, greedy decoding, Docker and an 8192-token limit; Appendix B.1 retains MBPP+ version 0.2.0.

E4.justification: The repository and file-generation cases, comparable-data-size comparisons, scaling experiments, leakage analysis, and complexity/diversity breakdowns are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the means, medians and standard deviations of code-complexity distributions in Table 12. Neither version adds run/seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and graphical findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains EpiCoder-Qwen-7B's 59.0 average and 27.7 BigCodeBench-Hard Complete score, while Table 8 retains its FullStackBench overall score of 50.24.

T1.justification: Equation (1), Algorithm 2's frequency-estimation formula and Appendix C.3's complexity formulas are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theoretical results, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about controllable diversity and complexity, benchmark performance, and potential repository-level synthesis. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of feature-tree control, data quality, scaling and leakage remain unchanged, as does the exploratory framing of repository synthesis. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: v2 lists the Microsoft EpiCoder repository. v3 retains that location and adds DeepLearnXMU/EpiCoder in the first-page code/data footnote. Implementation settings and appendix prompts are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5.1 and the bibliography remove Jiang et al. (2021a, 2021b) and Xie et al. (2021), leaving Sun et al. (2024) supporting the general code-intelligence background sentence. Positioning against code-data synthesis methods is otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises affiliations, internship annotations and correspondence information, adds an Acknowledgment section naming funding sources, and adjusts the abstract's access statement. The scientific prose and main section organization are otherwise preserved.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves from page 5 to page 6, while Figures 3–4 move from page 6 to page 5. Text and footnotes reflow, and code highlighting changes, but the figures, captions and table structures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 adds attribution/funding disclosures and a second repository pointer, while v2 already provided code/data access. The scientific explanation, experimental evidence, interpretations and appendix documentation are unchanged. These administrative updates, limited citation removals and layout adjustments leave the paper's overall clarity and evidential strength essentially unchanged.
